rounds.response:
Brief user-facing summary to add to the PR description and release notes:

This change makes shutdown perform a best-effort flush before exiting, with a configurable timeout SHUTDOWN_FLUSH_TIMEOUT_MS (default 1000 ms). Practically, this reduces intermittent data-corruption observed on abrupt shutdowns by waiting up to the configured time for in-flight data to be flushed, but it can add up to the configured value to shutdown latency. Operators can tune this behaviour by setting SHUTDOWN_FLUSH_TIMEOUT_MS (milliseconds) to a larger value to wait longer, or to 0 to disable the extra wait; if the flush does not complete within the timeout we abandon it and emit a warning log ("shutdown flush did not complete after {ms} ms"). Note this is a best-effort safeguard (not a guaranteed durability fix); increase the timeout if you observe recurring timeout warnings in logs.
